body:
The reviewed Calendar transform now collects hidden chunks once per synchronous pass, preserving reference identity, order, unchanged arrays and native geometry. It removes repeated growing-array copies and linear duplicate checks while retaining all DOM, the 1000-item grid bound, normal source reads and complete popups.

Quiet release whole-month profiles (1000 cards, 995 dated items, 44134 DOM elements, seven cold/warm samples per condition) improve local cold medians from 756-761 to 720-726 ms and constrained cold/warm medians by about 139-191 ms. Local warm readiness remains variable; no stable per-navigation guarantee is claimed. The ordinary three-day profile improves by about 4-6 ms locally and 12-27 ms constrained when warm.

The full gate passes 269 Rust, 142 JavaScript and 12 Python tests. Four release suites pass in Chromium and WebKit, including exact hidden counts, whole-month spans, full popup membership, resize, current versions and keyboard opening. The original manual app is rebuilt and restarted; all 59 prior resource versions, two pins, preferences and certificate are preserved, with trusted HTTPS and all 33 assets verified. Evidence: progress/2026-10-01-calendar-hidden-lists.md. Broader rendering, transport, concurrency, physical devices and release acceptance remain open.

metadata.summary: Verified linear hidden-list collection improves dense Calendar rendering.
